tagline: A shoreline road linking Waveland with a rebuilt Gulf park
intro: Beach Boulevard follows the shoreline through Waveland, connecting the city with Buccaneer State Park, Clermont Harbor and Lakeshore. Here the water is Mississippi Sound, an embayment of the Gulf of Mexico.

Hurricane Katrina changed the area’s transport connections in 2005. Rail damage suspended Amtrak service at Bay St. Louis; trains returned with the Mardi Gras Service in August 2025. The storm also badly damaged the US 90 bridge across the bay, and its replacement opened in 2007.

From Bay St. Louis, the journey continues into neighboring Waveland and along Beach Boulevard to Buccaneer State Park. The park straddles Waveland and Clermont Harbor; Beach Boulevard is Clermont Harbor’s main road in and out. Lakeshore lies at the western end of Hancock County.
notice: The US 90 bridge has a pedestrian and bicycle path on its Gulf side.

moments.title: Bay St. Louis
moments.text: The bridge across the bay is a replacement, part of the physical rebuilding after Hurricane Katrina. It carries US 90 between Bay St. Louis and Pass Christian, with four traffic lanes and a 12-foot path for pedestrians and cyclists on the Gulf side. The new crossing opened on May 17, 2007. Local artists’ work features in the pedestrian art walk. The town itself occupies the west side of the bay, which empties into Mississippi Sound. Katrina also interrupted the town’s rail service in 2005; passenger trains returned in 2025 with the New Orleans–Mobile Mardi Gras Service.
moments.notice: Local artists’ work appears along the bridge’s pedestrian art walk.

moments.title: Waveland
moments.text: Waveland’s Civic and Cultural Center was the city’s only public building left standing after Hurricane Katrina. In 2013 it became home to the Ground Zero Hurricane Museum. The city had already endured a long recovery after Camille struck in 1969, heavily damaging the area south of the Louisville and Nashville Railroad. That recovery lasted nearly a decade. After Camille, the town erected a plaque recognizing volunteers who had supplied labor and resources for rebuilding. Katrina again devastated the area south of the railway in 2005, and the public library was gutted, requiring a complete rebuild.

moments.title: Buccaneer State Park
moments.text: Every building in Buccaneer State Park was destroyed by Hurricane Katrina in 2005; the Gulf-side park was entirely rebuilt. Its land has an earlier connection to Andrew Jackson, who lived and owned property on what is now Jackson Ridge in Waveland. Much of that ridge later became the park. The recreation area straddles Waveland and Clermont Harbor, off Beach Boulevard. Its facilities include a waterpark, campgrounds and a 1.8-mile nature trail.
